goal: 在数据讨论会上清晰讲解图表数据,并从容回应与会者的质疑

n1.speaker: 部门主管 Ms. Grant
n1.line: Thank you all for coming. Let us begin with the quarterly chart in front of you. Could you walk us through the overall trend at a glance?
n1.lineCn: 感谢各位出席。我们先来看大家面前的季度图表。你能带我们一眼看出总体趋势吗?

grammar.name: Walk us through
grammar.note: 口语化但正式的图表讲解指令:walk through 意为“逐项讲解”,后面接图表或数据。

options.text: Certainly. As you can see, revenue climbed steadily over the first two quarters, then levelled off in the third before surging again in December.
options.textCn: 当然。大家可以看到,营收前两季度稳步攀升,第三季度趋于平稳,十二月再次激增。
options.feedback: climb steadily、level off、surge 等图表动词精准连贯,开头就抓人。

options.text: So the line goes up, then it goes flat, and then it goes up a lot at the end.
options.textCn: 线先是往上走,然后走平,最后又涨了很多。
options.feedback: goes up、goes flat 太随意,缺少图表描述的核心动词,与会者听不出细节。

options.text: The chart is a bit complicated, so I will just read out the numbers one by one.
options.textCn: 图表有点复杂,我就一个数字一个数字念吧。
options.feedback: 逐个数念数字无法呈现趋势,说明你还没有抓住数据的主干。

n2.speaker: 同事 A (运营部 Tom)
n2.line: I can see the December surge, but what accounts for the sharp fluctuation between October and November?
n2.lineCn: 我看到了十二月的激增,但十月到十一月之间的剧烈波动是什么原因?

grammar.name: What accounts for...?
grammar.note: 图表讨论中追问原因的句式:account for 表示“解释、占……比例”,比 ask why 更专业。

options.text: Good question. The dip in November corresponds to the warehouse relocation, after which sales recovered sharply once inventory was restored.
options.textCn: 好问题。十一月下滑对应仓库搬迁,库存恢复后销售迅速反弹。
options.feedback: 用 corresponds to 建立因果,再以 recovered sharply 交代反弹,有因有果。

options.text: I am not sure, the data is the data, maybe it was just a bad month.
options.textCn: 我不确定,数据就是这样,也许就是那个月不行吧。
options.feedback: 无法解释关键波动,等于承认没有分析,与会者信心大跌。

options.text: The fluctuation was mainly attributable to a delivery backlog, which we resolved by December.
options.textCn: 波动主要归因于配送积压,我们在十二月解决了这一问题。
options.feedback: attributable to 归因表达专业,与后续回升形成闭环。

n3.speaker: 部门主管 Ms. Grant
n3.line: Let us try again with more precise language. Describe the trend using the standard expressions for rises, falls and stability.
n3.lineCn: 我们再用更精确的语言试一次。请用描述上升、下降和平稳的标准表达来讲趋势。

grammar.name: Standard expressions for trends
grammar.note: 图表题高频动词库:rise/increase/climb (上升), drop/decline/plunge (下降), level off/remain stable (平稳)。

options.text: Revenue rose moderately from January to June, remained fairly stable through autumn, and rose dramatically in December.
options.textCn: 营收一月到六月温和上升,秋季保持相当平稳,十二月急剧上涨。
options.feedback: moderately、fairly stable、dramatically 等程度副词加动词,图表语合格。

options.text: It went up a bit, stayed the same for a while, then went up lots.
options.textCn: 涨了一点,平稳了一阵子,然后又大涨。
options.feedback: a bit、went up lots 无法满足图表描述的精确要求,仍然不合格。

options.text: I see the trend as: a gentle incline, a plateau, and finally a sharp peak in December.
options.textCn: 我看到的趋势是:平缓爬升、一段平台期,最后十二月出现陡峭峰值。
options.feedback: incline、plateau、peak 三个名词精准概括全图,表达非常老练。

n4.speaker: 同事 B (财务部 Nina)
n4.line: You call December a peak, yet December sales account for nearly a third of the whole year. Is that peak really sustainable, or is it a one-off?
n4.lineCn: 你说十二月是峰值,可十二月销售额占了全年近三分之一。这个峰值真的可持续,还是昙花一现?

grammar.name: Account for
grammar.note: account for 的另一个高频义:“占(比例)”。December sales account for a third of the year 即“占全年的三分之一”。

options.text: A fair challenge. The December figure largely reflects promotional campaigns; without them, underlying demand has been rising by roughly two per cent quarterly.
options.textCn: 质疑有理。十二月数字主要来自促销活动;剔除后,基础需求每季度约增长百分之二。
options.feedback: 拆分促销因素与基础需求,说明你读懂了数据背后的构成。

options.text: It is sustainable, I am confident about that, because December is always our best month.
options.textCn: 可持续的,我对此很有信心,因为十二月向来是我们最好的月份。
options.feedback: 用“向来如此”代替分析,没有回应占比异常背后的结构问题。

options.text: I would distinguish seasonal spikes from the underlying trend; the latter has grown consistently at about two per cent per quarter.
options.textCn: 我会把季节性峰值与基础趋势区分开;后者每季度稳定增长约百分之二。
options.feedback: 用 distinguish... from 区分概念,再看基础趋势,分析层次分明。

n5.speaker: 同事 A (运营部 Tom)
n5.line: Let me restate the question: do you have an explanation for the November dip that connects to the surrounding data?
n5.lineCn: 我换种方式问:你能结合前后数据解释十一月下滑的原因吗?

grammar.name: Connect to the surrounding data
grammar.note: 数据讨论中的核心要求:任何解释都应 connect to (联系) 前后数据,不能孤立看单点。

options.text: Yes. The dip coincides with the warehouse move in November, and the recovery in December supports that link.
options.textCn: 能。下滑与十一月仓库搬迁时间吻合,而十二月的回升也支持这一关联。
options.feedback: 用 coincides with 加时间对照,证据链完整,质疑得到解决。

options.text: I do not have an explanation, honestly. It is just what the chart shows.
options.textCn: 说实话,我没有解释。图表显示什么就是什么。
options.feedback: 两次被问仍无法解释关键波动,数据分析能力受到严重质疑。

options.text: The dip aligns with a supply disruption; once shipments resumed, the figures rebounded accordingly.
options.textCn: 下滑与供应链中断一致;运输恢复后,数据也相应反弹。
options.feedback: aligns with 与 rebounded accordingly 前后呼应,逻辑自洽。

n6.speaker: 同事 C (市场部 Leo)
n6.line: Looking at the pie chart beside it, online sales account for forty per cent of the total. How does that share compare with last year?
n6.lineCn: 看旁边的饼图,线上销售占总量的四成。这个占比和去年相比如何?

grammar.name: How does X compare with Y?
grammar.note: 比较句式:compare with 表示“与……相比”,图表讨论中用于追问变化幅度。

options.text: The share has expanded considerably, from roughly a quarter last year to forty per cent now, overtaking brick-and-mortar sales for the first time.
options.textCn: 占比大幅扩大,从去年约四分之一增至现在的四成,首次超过实体店销售。
options.feedback: 用具体数字加 overtake 的对比,既答了比例又讲了变化,信息量大。

options.text: It is bigger than last year, I think, which is good news.
options.textCn: 比去年大,我觉得,这是好消息。
options.feedback: 没给出具体对比数据,“我觉得”也削弱了陈述的客观性。

options.text: Online has grown from twenty-six per cent to forty per cent, at the expense of physical channels, which dropped correspondingly.
options.textCn: 线上从百分之二十六增至百分之四十,以实体渠道相应下滑为代价。
options.feedback: 数字精确,at the expense of 与 correspondingly 交代了此消彼长的关系。

n7.speaker: 部门主管 Ms. Grant
n7.line: Finally, given the current trajectory, what projection would you make for the next quarter, and on what grounds?
n7.lineCn: 最后,按目前的走势,你对下季度作何预测?依据是什么?

grammar.name: On what grounds
grammar.note: on... grounds 表示“以……为依据”,追问预测依据时比 why 更书面。

options.text: I project moderate growth, barring any supply disruption, since the underlying demand trend has remained steady for five consecutive quarters.
options.textCn: 除非供应链中断,我预计温和增长,因为基础需求趋势已连续五个季度保持稳定。
options.feedback: barring 条件限定加连续数据支撑,预测审慎而可信。

options.text: I predict sales will keep going up, because they usually do.
options.textCn: 我预测销售会继续涨,因为通常都涨。
options.feedback: “因为通常都涨”缺乏依据,预测等于猜测,主管只能结束会议。

options.text: Provided the promotional calendar is maintained, I expect a repeat of last December's performance, with growth concentrated in the final month.
options.textCn: 只要促销日程保持,我预计会重现去年十二月的情形,增长集中在最后一个月。
options.feedback: provided 条件句加增长分布预测,展现出对数据模式的理解。

n8.speaker: 同事 B (财务部 Nina)
n8.line: One last check: are these figures drawn from the audited system, or from the preliminary report?
n8.lineCn: 最后确认一点:这些数字来自已审计的系统,还是初步报告?

grammar.name: Drawn from
grammar.note: be drawn from 表示“取自、来源于”,数据讨论中交代数据来源的规范说法。

options.text: They are drawn from the audited system; I can circulate the source tables after the meeting.
options.textCn: 数据取自已审计系统;会后我可以把源表格发给大家。
options.feedback: 来源明确且主动提供凭证,数据可信度无可指摘,会议圆满结束。

options.text: I honestly do not remember which system they came from.
options.textCn: 老实说我不记得数据是从哪个系统来的。
options.feedback: 连数据来源都不清楚,之前所有分析的可靠性都打上问号。

options.text: They come from the official system, and the audit team verified them last week.
options.textCn: 来自官方系统,审计团队上周已核验过。
options.feedback: 补充审计核验信息,进一步巩固数据的可信度。

success.speaker: 部门主管 Ms. Grant
success.line: Excellent work. Your grasp of the data is clear, and the team will adopt your projection for the budget review.
success.lineCn: 干得漂亮。你对数据的把握很清晰,团队将在预算评审中采纳你的预测。

grammar.name: Grasp of the data
grammar.note: 固定搭配:a grasp of 表示“对……的把握”,常修饰 data、concept 等抽象名词。

fail1.speaker: 部门主管 Ms. Grant
fail1.line: I am afraid we cannot rely on this analysis today. Please rework the figures and present them with proper chart language at the next meeting.
fail1.lineCn: 恐怕我们今天无法采信这份分析。请重新整理数据,下次会议用规范的图表语言汇报。

grammar.name: Cannot rely on
grammar.note: rely on 表示“依赖、采信”,否定式 cannot rely on 在职场表达中常用于否决一项工作成果。

fail2.speaker: 同事 B (财务部 Nina)
fail2.line: Without solid answers to these questions, the numbers cannot be taken at face value. We shall need a further review.
fail2.lineCn: 这些问题得不到可靠回答,数字就不能只看表面。我们需要进一步审查。

grammar.name: At face value
grammar.note: 固定短语 at face value 表示“按表面价值相信”,常用于质疑数据的可信度。
